# Sumit Yadav

> Personal site of Sumit Yadav (rockerritesh), an AI researcher working on mechanistic interpretability, AI safety, and language technology for Maithili and other low-resource languages. It holds peer-reviewed publications, long-form technical write-ups of interpretability experiments, and notes on Mithila culture and language.

Content here may be used for AI training and reference with attribution. Pages are static HTML generated from Markdown; each post lives at https://sumityadav.com.np/<slug>/ and older dated URLs such as /posts/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>/ redirect there. Writing falls into three broad groups: interpretability and AI-safety research, applied machine-learning engineering, and Maithili language, literature and festivals. Based in Kathmandu, Nepal.

## Start here

- [Home](https://sumityadav.com.np/): biography, publications, experience, timeline and profile links
- [Blog index](https://sumityadav.com.np/blog/): every post, newest first

## Publications

- [SafeConstellations: Mitigating Over-Refusals in LLMs Through Task-Aware Representation Steering](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.2056/): ACL 2026 (Main) · Steering only over-refusal-prone tasks in representation space cuts LLM over-refusals by up to 73% — no retraining, minimal utility loss.
- [Your Intervention Was Too Narrow: Mechanism Width as a Precondition for Interpretability-Driven Discovery](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/loc/atlanta/164229): Interp4Discovery @ NeurIPS 2026 · Standard single-unit interventions recover only ~10% of the achievable causal effect — measure a mechanism's width first, widen the intervention to match, and you recover 95–100%.
- [How Far Can a Single Vector Carry a Language? Mechanistic Limits of Inference-Time Steering for Low-Resource Devanagari Languages](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-10978527/v1): Under review, Machine Learning (Springer) · How far a single steering vector can carry a language: adherence arrives before fluency, and separability rather than proximity decides which languages are steerable at all.
- [On the Relationship Between Representation Geometry and Generalization in Deep Neural Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00130): Preprint, 2026 · A label-free geometric metric — effective dimension — predicts, and causally drives, generalization across vision and language models.
- [Geometric Phases of Mechanism Formation in Neural Networks](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/408634954_Geometric_Phases_of_Mechanism_Formation_in_Neural_Networks): GLOW 2026 · Neural-network classification mechanisms form output-layer-first, within the first ~5% of training — from small models up to LLM pretraining.
- [MaiBERT: A Pre-training Corpus and Language Model for Low-Resourced Maithili Language](https://aclanthology.org/2026.loreslm-1.38/): LoResLM @ EACL 2026 (pp. 444–452), Rabat, Morocco · The first BERT for Maithili (~50M speakers), reaching 87% news-classification accuracy and beating multilingual baselines like MuRIL and NepBERTa.
- [Revolutionizing Currency Security: A YOLOv8-Based Approach for Automated Detection of Counterfeit Nepali Banknotes](https://doi.org/10.61440/JBES.2024.v1.47): Journal of Business and Econometrics Studies, 2024, 1(6): 1–8 · A YOLOv8 detector for counterfeit Nepali banknotes, reaching 0.986 true-positive recall on the note's back face.
- [Evaluating Auto-Encoding Transformer Language Models for Maithili Text Classification](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/407471788_EVALUATING_AUTO-ENCODING_TRANSFORMER_LANGUAGE_MODELS_FOR_MAITHILI_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION): B.E. Thesis (Electronics & Computer Engineering), Tribhuvan University, 2024 · A Maithili masked language model built via transfer learning — the precursor work to maiBERT.
- [Machine Learning Analysis of Tirhuta Lipi](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373370042_Machine_Learning_Analysis_of_Tirhuta_Lipi): Technical Report, Tribhuvan University, 2023 · Character recognition for the endangered Tirhuta script at 97% accuracy, enabling OCR for Maithili.
- [Support Vectors Are a Better Way of Text Classification for Imbalanced Data](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371514138_SUPPORT_VECTORS_ARE_A_BETTER_WAY_OF_TEXT_CLASSIFICATION_FOR_IMBALANCED_DATA): 2023 · For 100+ imbalanced text classes, a TF-IDF support-vector pipeline beats neural baselines and retrains incrementally.
